scenario_text: A charged particle enters a uniform magnetic field region and experiences a velocity-dependent transverse force while a fixed background of collisional drag slightly damps its motion. The particle's velocity components in the plane perpendicular to the field evolve over time as the magnetic deflection continuously redirects its momentum. The weak drag acts only as a fixed damping background and not as the primary mechanism. We track how the in-plane velocity components change.

spec.target_description: Rate of change of the x-component of the particle's velocity in the plane perpendicular to the magnetic field.

required_dynamic_states.description: Velocity component along x perpendicular to the field.
Velocity component along y perpendicular to the field.

scenario_text: A capacitor discharges through a resistor in a simple loop, and the stored charge decreases as current flows. The charge on the capacitor plates governs the potential that drives the current through the resistor. We follow the charge over time as the loop dissipates the stored energy. The resistor and capacitor values are fixed conditions.

spec.target_description: Rate of change of charge stored on the capacitor plates.

required_dynamic_states.description: Charge stored on the capacitor plates.

scenario_text: The electric field magnitude from a small charged sphere is measured at various radial distances in free space. The distance from the sphere center sets the strength of the observed field. Experimenters sample distances and record the instantaneous field magnitude. The sphere charge is held fixed.

spec.target_description: Electric field magnitude measured at a given radial distance from the charged sphere.

input_symbols.description: Radial distance from the sphere center.

scenario_text: A series loop containing inductance, resistance, and capacitance is driven by an oscillating source, and the current amplitude at steady state depends on the drive frequency. Sweeping the drive frequency produces a peaked response near the natural resonance. The component values are fixed and the amplitude is read after transients settle. We record the steady-state current amplitude versus frequency.

spec.target_description: Steady-state current amplitude in the driven series loop at a given drive frequency.

input_symbols.description: Angular drive frequency of the source.

scenario_text: An oscillating charge radiates and the time-averaged radiated power depends on the frequency of oscillation and the amplitude of charge motion. Experimenters sample oscillation frequency and displacement amplitude and record the emitted power. The charge magnitude is fixed. The measurement is instantaneous averaged output.

spec.target_description: Time-averaged power radiated by the oscillating charge.

input_symbols.description: Angular oscillation frequency of the charge.

scenario_text: An inductor in series with a resistor is connected to a constant voltage source, and the current builds up as the inductor opposes changes in current. The instantaneous current sets the voltage split between the inductor and resistor. We track the current as it rises toward its final value. The source voltage and component values are fixed.

spec.target_description: Rate of change of current through the series inductor-resistor loop.

required_dynamic_states.description: Current flowing through the inductor and resistor.

scenario_text: A plane electromagnetic wave propagates through a slightly conductive medium and its field amplitude diminishes with penetration depth. The remaining amplitude at a given depth sets the local energy carried further. Experimenters measure amplitude at sampled depths for different medium conductivities. The incident amplitude is fixed.

spec.target_description: Wave field amplitude at a given penetration depth into the conductive medium.

scenario_text: Two parallel current-carrying wires separated by an adjustable gap exert a force per unit length on each other. The separation distance and the currents determine the instantaneous force magnitude. Experimenters vary the separation and one current and read the force. The wires are held rigid.

spec.target_description: Force per unit length between the two parallel current-carrying wires.

scenario_text: A nonlinear circuit element with cubic voltage-current behavior is combined with an inductor and capacitor to form a self-sustaining oscillator. The capacitor voltage and inductor current jointly evolve, with the nonlinear element supplying energy at low amplitude and removing it at high amplitude. We follow the capacitor voltage over time as a stable oscillation emerges. The element parameters are fixed background settings.

spec.target_description: Rate of change of the capacitor voltage in the nonlinear oscillator.
forbidden_behaviors: decay to zero for all initial conditions

scenario_text: A dielectric slab is placed between capacitor plates, and its polarization aligns partially with the applied field but saturates as the field grows large. The applied field strength sets the induced polarization density. Experimenters sample field strengths and measure the resulting polarization. The dielectric type is fixed.

spec.target_description: Induced polarization density in the dielectric at a given applied field strength.

input_symbols.description: Applied electric field strength across the slab.
Saturation polarization limit of the material.

expected_behaviors: approach to saturation at high field

scenario_text: A cart of fixed mass slides along a horizontal track while a resistive drag proportional to the square of its speed opposes its motion. No propulsion is applied after release, so the cart gradually decelerates. Engineers track how the velocity decays along the trajectory from an initial launch speed. The goal is to model how the instantaneous speed changes over time.

spec.target_description: Rate of change of the cart's speed under quadratic drag.

required_dynamic_states.description: Instantaneous speed of the cart along the track.

scenario_text: A small block is attached to a spring on a frictionless surface and displaced from its rest position. Once released, the restoring force pulls it back and it moves back and forth about equilibrium. The system exchanges kinetic and potential energy without loss. We follow the block's position over time from its initial displacement and velocity.

spec.target_description: Rate of change of the block's displacement in the spring system.

required_dynamic_states.description: Displacement of the block from equilibrium.

scenario_text: A pendulum bob hangs from a pivot and is released from a moderately large angle where the small-angle approximation fails. The gravitational torque drives it swinging back and forth along an arc. The motion remains undamped in this idealized study. We follow the angular displacement over time starting from the release angle at rest.

spec.target_description: Rate of change of the pendulum's angular displacement.

required_dynamic_states.description: Angular displacement of the pendulum from vertical.

scenario_text: A hanging mass on a spring is subject to viscous damping and slowly settles toward its resting position after an initial pull. The damping strength is large enough that the mass returns to equilibrium without overshooting. Motion proceeds from the initial stretch and starting velocity. We track how the displacement relaxes over time.

spec.target_description: Rate of change of displacement for the overdamped mass-spring system.

required_dynamic_states.description: Displacement of the mass from equilibrium.

scenario_text: A solid uniform sphere released on an inclined ramp rolls down without slipping. The gravitational component along the incline drives translation while rotational inertia resists acceleration. The steady-state acceleration depends on the incline angle and the object's mass distribution factor. We predict the linear acceleration as a function of the fixed experimental conditions.

spec.target_description: Linear acceleration of a rolling body down the incline.

input_symbols.description: Incline angle from horizontal in radians.
Moment-of-inertia shape factor (I divided by m r squared).

expected_behaviors: acceleration decreases for larger shape factor

scenario_text: Two point masses interact under mutual gravitational attraction, and a light satellite is placed in a circular orbit around the heavier body. The orbital speed required to maintain a stable circular path depends on the central mass and the orbital radius. Experimenters vary these conditions and measure the needed speed. The objective is to model the circular orbital speed.

spec.target_description: Speed required for a stable circular orbit.

input_symbols.description: Orbital radius from the central body.

scenario_text: A block rests on a horizontal surface and is pushed by a steadily increasing horizontal force. As long as the applied force stays below the static friction limit the block does not move, but once the threshold is exceeded it begins to accelerate under kinetic friction. The net driving force therefore behaves differently in the two regimes. We model the net accelerating force as a function of the applied push.

spec.target_description: Net horizontal force available to accelerate the block.

input_symbols.description: Normal force pressing the block to the surface.

expected_behaviors: zero net force below the static threshold
positive net force once sliding begins
forbidden_behaviors: smooth linear response through the threshold

scenario_text: A projectile is launched into the air and experiences both gravity and linear air resistance proportional to velocity. The vertical velocity evolves as gravity pulls downward while drag opposes motion. Over time the descent tends toward a limiting sink rate. We follow the vertical velocity from an upward launch.

spec.target_description: Rate of change of the vertical velocity under gravity and linear drag.
expected_behaviors: approach to a terminal sink rate

scenario_text: A flywheel of fixed rotational inertia is spun up by a constant driving torque while a speed-proportional bearing friction resists rotation. The angular velocity rises and eventually levels off at a steady spin rate. Motion is followed from an initial angular velocity. We model how the angular velocity changes over time.

spec.target_description: Rate of change of the flywheel's angular velocity.
expected_behaviors: rise toward a steady spin rate

scenario_text: A ball is dropped and bounces repeatedly on a hard floor, losing a fixed fraction of its speed at each impact due to an imperfect restitution. The maximum rebound height therefore decreases from one bounce to the next. Experimenters record the peak height reached after a given number of bounces. We model the rebound peak height as a function of the bounce count and conditions.

spec.target_description: Peak rebound height after a given number of bounces.
